paras: The threatened lynching of Fayette Hardee took place at Vaiden, Mississippi, on the night of October 7, 1881, when Hardee, a Black man, was found under the bed of a woman described as a "highly respectable young lady" and was suspected of intending to steal. According to a Dallas newspaper, a crowd "came very near lynching him," but he was not reported harmed.

On the night of the 7th, Hardee, described as "colored," was found upstairs in a house at Vaiden, under the bed of a young woman the papers called "highly respectable." Both accounts said he was thought to have been there to steal, though neither reports a theft or anything taken. The Dallas Herald added that "a crowd came very near lynching him," without saying who the crowd were, how many gathered, or what stopped them.
No report of an arrest, charge or trial of Hardee, or of any action against the crowd, appears in the coverage.

The Dallas Daily Herald printed the story on October 12 as a single sentence in its "News Nuggets" column of regional briefs, calling Hardee "a negro" and spelling the town "Vaden." The Dallas Weekly Herald repeated the item word for word the next day. In Mississippi, the Weekly Panola Star of October 15 gave the date and the spelling "Vaiden" but framed the episode as a joke, opening, "At last one woman has been rewarded for looking under the bed," and said nothing of a crowd or a lynching. Neither paper commented on the near-lynching itself.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of Fayette Hardee
bases: The only report of violence is the Dallas brief's statement that a crowd 'came very near lynching' Hardee after he was found under a young woman's bed, a threatened lynching (A1).
Hardee was not killed; a crowd reportedly came 'very near lynching him' over a suspected theft, which makes this a threatened lynching only (A1), and the Panola Star mentions no crowd at all (A3).
Two Dallas Herald editions (A1, A2, one item) and the Panola Star (A3) agree that Hardee was found under the bed, but only the Herald item reports the crowd's near-lynching.

accounts.label: Dallas Herald 'News Nuggets' brief
accounts.gist: A negro named Fayette Hardee was found under a young lady's bed at Vaden, Mississippi, it was thought for theft, and a crowd came very near lynching him.

accounts.gist: At Vaiden on the night of the 7th, Fayette Hardee, colored, was found upstairs under a young lady's bed and was believed to be there to steal; nothing is said of a crowd.

framing.detail: The Dallas Herald gave it one sentence among unrelated regional briefs, noting the near-lynching without comment.
